### The five things to hunt for specifically

- **Tense.** Copy written before opening and never updated ("will boast…"). An established
  business still describing itself in future tense is the single most damning find.
- **Self-contradictions.** Hours, phone numbers, addresses and counts that disagree between
  two pages, or between a body section and the footer. Check every page against every page.
- **Pages that don't do what they're named.** An "Events Calendar" that is really a private
  booking form, with no public listing anywhere.
- **Buried real assets.** A useful landmark in a footer, real specs, real hiring copy, real
  application fields — things worth surfacing, not inventing.
- **Dead-end journeys.** Pages barely linked, forms with no way to actually apply or submit.

Audit the market, not just the client. The strongest pitch line on the last build came from
discovering the only comparable venue had no website of its own.

## Pitch lines this audit produced

Frame around growth, never around blame — "your site hasn't kept up with how much you've
grown," not "you got ripped off." The owner may still value that relationship.
